subject.title: fix(doctor): exit non-zero on final invalid config (#77804)

question: Should plain human-oriented `openclaw doctor` return exit code 1 when its final persisted config is invalid, or should non-zero configuration gating remain exclusive to the documented `doctor --lint` automation surface?
rationale: Both policies are technically viable, but changing the existing plain-doctor exit contract can break wrappers and upgrade workflows, so repository product intent—not implementation inference—must choose the permanent behavior.

options.title: Keep Automation Lint-Only
options.body: Preserve the existing plain-doctor exit contract, direct scripts to `doctor --lint`, and close or narrow this PR to a separately approved human-facing output improvement.

options.title: Approve Plain-Doctor Failure
options.body: Accept the compatibility change, update the Doctor documentation, and require real built-CLI proof for valid, invalid, and successfully repaired configurations before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep Automation Lint-Only
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing plain-doctor exit contract, direct scripts to `doctor --lint`, and close or narrow this PR to a separately approved human-facing output improvement.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes a public CLI and upgrade-facing contract spanning Doctor, configuration, and release behavior.
